intro: You can already present, take part in meetings and talk about how long you've been doing something. Now you'll use all of that in a **job interview**: describe your experience with concrete examples and numbers, answer 'Tell me about a time …' questions with the **STAR method**, and talk about your strengths, a weakness and your career goals. Warm-up: what's one thing at work or on campus that you're proud of?
teachingNotes: This functional lesson builds on b1-present-perfect and b1-present-perfect-continuous (for + a length of time, since + a starting point; I've been working as … for …), b1-vocab-work-education (apply for, CV / résumé, interview, experience is uncountable, good at), b2-vocab-work-business (be responsible for, increase / decrease by + amount, KPI, on track), b1-telling-stories (past simple for events, past continuous for the background) and b2-presentations (clear structure, numbers explained simply). Recap those in a line; don't re-teach them. New here: describing experience with proof (I was responsible for …, I managed to …, results with numbers), the STAR method for behavioural questions, and strengths, weaknesses, career goals and questions to ask the interviewer. Contexts: a bank in Surabaya, an e-commerce company in Jakarta, a clinic, a startup; interviews in Indonesia and abroad (online with a company in Singapore or Sydney).

Experience: 'Tell me about yourself' = now (I've been working as a … for / since …) → before (Before that, I worked at …) → why this job. The node's common error is *'I have worked here since three years' → 'I have worked here for three years': three years is a length (for), 2022 is a starting point (since). Both 'I've worked here for three years' and 'I've been working here for three years' are correct: never make them compete. Proof phrases: I was responsible for + noun / -ing (not *responsible to); I managed to + verb (= berhasil; not *'I succeeded to', which is a common Indonesian error from 'berhasil'; 'I succeeded in + -ing' is correct but formal); I led / managed a team of five (manage + noun = memimpin, mengelola: a different meaning from managed to); results with by + amount: reduced costs by 15%, increased sales by 20%. Experience stays uncountable: *'many experiences in marketing' → five years of experience in marketing. per cent (British) / percent (American).

STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) is a way to answer behavioural questions (pertanyaan tentang perilakumu di masa lalu): Tell me about a time when you … / Give me an example of … / Describe a situation when you …. S = the background, short (when, where, your role); T = what you had to do or solve; A = what YOU did, step by step: the longest part; R = what happened in the end, with numbers if possible, plus what you learnt. Grammar: past simple for the events, past continuous for the background (I was working as …). Say I, not we, for your own actions: many Indonesians say 'kami' / 'tim kami' to be modest, but the interviewer wants to know what you did (Our team …, and I personally …). Traps: present tense in the story (*'Last year our app crash, so I call the developer'), a long Situation and no Result. behavioural (British) / behavioral (American); learnt (British) / learned (both).

Strengths, weaknesses, goals: My main strength is + noun (problem-solving, teamwork) or that + sentence; then prove it: For example, …. A weakness should be real, not a disaster for this job, and come with what you're doing about it (present continuous / present perfect continuous: I'm working on it; I've been taking an online course). 'I'm a perfectionist' is a cliché interviewers hear a lot: a tendency, don't mark it wrong, but ask for a real example. Goals: In five years, I'd like to … / I'm hoping to … / My long-term goal is to … (I want to … is understandable but less polite). Questions to ask: What does a typical day look like in this role? / What are the biggest challenges for the team right now? / What are the next steps in the process? Saying 'No, I don't have any questions' can sound uninterested. Salary and leave usually come later or when the interviewer raises them: a tendency, varies by company and country.

Indonesian interview habits, named respectfully (they are polite in Indonesian culture, they just send a different message in English): excessive modesty (the 'saya masih belajar' style: Sorry, my English is not good, I'm still learning, I'm just a normal staff) can sound like you lack skills or confidence; overclaiming (I'm the best, I can do everything, I'm expert in all software) is hard to believe. The middle way: facts and numbers. 'I'm still learning about X' is fine if you follow it with what you can already do. Indonesian CVs and interviews often include religion, marital status, age and a photo; in many countries (the UK, the US, Australia) interviewers usually avoid these topics because hiring shouldn't depend on them, so you don't need to mention them unprompted. If an Indonesian interviewer asks, a short polite answer is fine.

Limits: A0–B1 grammar plus the chain (no third conditional, wish, past modals like should have, participle clauses, non-defining relative clauses, causative, future perfect or advanced passive). Don't teach CV or cover-letter writing, salary negotiation or formal interview etiquette in depth. Listening items use one voice and no speaker labels. Correct one thing at a time, usually since three years, succeeded to, responsible to, many experiences, or we instead of I.

keyPoints.title: Describe your experience with proof
keyPoints.explanation: Say how long with for (a length) or since (a starting point): I've been working as a nurse for six years / since 2019 (not 'since six years'). Then give proof: I was responsible for the company's social media. I managed to (berhasil) cut costs by 15%. I led a team of five. Numbers and results make your experience believable: increased sales by 20%, trained 40 new staff. Experience is uncountable: five years of experience, not 'many experiences'.

examples.id: Saya sudah bekerja sebagai desainer grafis selama empat tahun.

examples.en: In my last job, I was responsible for the online shop's customer service.
examples.id: Di pekerjaan saya sebelumnya, saya bertanggung jawab atas layanan pelanggan toko online.

id.title: Menjelaskan pengalamanmu dengan bukti
id.explanation: Sebutkan berapa lama dengan for (lamanya) atau since (titik mulainya): I've been working as a nurse for six years / since 2019 (bukan 'since six years'). Lalu beri bukti: I was responsible for the company's social media (bertanggung jawab atas). I managed to (berhasil) cut costs by 15%. I led a team of five (memimpin tim berisi lima orang). Angka dan hasil membuat pengalamanmu meyakinkan: increased sales by 20%, trained 40 new staff. Experience (pengalaman kerja) tidak bisa dihitung: five years of experience, bukan 'many experiences'.

keyPoints.title: Answer behavioural questions with STAR
keyPoints.explanation: Behavioural questions ask what you did in a real situation: Tell me about a time when you …. Answer in four parts. Situation: the background, short. Task: what you had to do. Action: what you did, step by step (the longest part). Result: what happened in the end, with numbers if possible, and what you learnt. Tell it in the past simple, and say I, not we, for your own actions.

examples.en: Last year, I was working as an admin supervisor at a clinic in Surabaya.
examples.id: Tahun lalu, saya bekerja sebagai supervisor admin di sebuah klinik di Surabaya.

examples.en: First, I looked at the data, and then I moved two staff to the morning shift.
examples.id: Pertama, saya melihat datanya, lalu saya memindahkan dua staf ke shift pagi.

examples.en: As a result, the waiting time fell from 70 to 25 minutes.
examples.id: Hasilnya, waktu tunggu turun dari 70 menjadi 25 menit.

id.title: Menjawab pertanyaan perilaku dengan STAR
id.explanation: Pertanyaan perilaku (behavioural questions) menanyakan apa yang kamu lakukan dalam situasi nyata: Tell me about a time when you … (ceritakan saat kamu …). Jawab dalam empat bagian. Situation: latar belakangnya, singkat. Task: apa yang harus kamu lakukan. Action: apa yang kamu lakukan, langkah demi langkah (bagian terpanjang). Result: apa yang terjadi pada akhirnya, dengan angka kalau bisa, dan apa yang kamu pelajari. Ceritakan dengan past simple, dan pakai I, bukan we, untuk tindakanmu sendiri.

keyPoints.title: Strengths, weaknesses and career goals
keyPoints.explanation: Name one strength and prove it: My main strength is problem-solving. For example, …. For a weakness, choose something real and say how you're improving: I sometimes find it hard to say no, so I'm learning to agree on priorities with my manager. For goals: In five years, I'd like to … / I'm hoping to …. At the end, ask the interviewer a question: What does a typical day look like in this role? Be confident with facts: not too modest ('I'm still learning, I'm nobody'), not too proud ('I'm the best').

examples.en: My main strength is attention to detail. For example, I check every invoice twice before I send it.
examples.id: Kekuatan utama saya adalah ketelitian. Contohnya, saya mengecek setiap tagihan dua kali sebelum mengirimnya.

examples.en: In five years, I'm hoping to lead a small data team.
examples.id: Dalam lima tahun, saya berharap bisa memimpin tim data kecil.

examples.en: What are the biggest challenges for the team right now?
examples.id: Apa tantangan terbesar tim saat ini?

id.title: Kekuatan, kelemahan dan tujuan karier
id.explanation: Sebutkan satu kekuatan lalu buktikan: My main strength is problem-solving. For example, …. Untuk kelemahan, pilih sesuatu yang nyata dan katakan bagaimana kamu memperbaikinya: I sometimes find it hard to say no, so I'm learning to agree on priorities with my manager. Untuk tujuan: In five years, I'd like to … / I'm hoping to …. Di akhir, ajukan pertanyaan kepada pewawancara: What does a typical day look like in this role? Percaya dirilah dengan fakta: jangan terlalu merendah ('I'm still learning, I'm nobody'), jangan juga terlalu membanggakan diri ('I'm the best').

assessment.prompt: In an interview at a bank in Surabaya, Dimas says this sentence, but it has a mistake. Write the correct sentence: I've been working here since six years.
acceptableAnswers: i've been working here for six years
i have been working here for six years
i've been working here for 6 years
i have been working here for 6 years
i've worked here for six years
i have worked here for six years
i've worked here for 6 years
i have worked here for 6 years
assessment.rubric: Correct: I've been working here for six years (six years is a length of time → for; since is for a starting point). 'I've worked here for six years' is also correct = 100. A sentence with since + a real starting point (since 2019) = 70 (correct English, but it changes the information). 'I'm working here for six years' or 'I work here for six years' = 30 (for is fixed, but the present perfect is lost). Unchanged 'since six years' = 0.

assessment.prompt: In your last job, getting 200 new customers in three months was hard, but you did it. Complete with one word that means 'berhasil': After a lot of hard work, I ___ to get 200 new customers in three months.
acceptableAnswers: managed
assessment.rubric: Correct: managed (managed to + verb = berhasil). 'was able' (two words) = 90 (correct meaning). 'succeeded' = 30 (a common error from 'berhasil': succeed takes in + -ing, I succeeded in getting …, not 'succeeded to'). 'tried' = 20 (it doesn't say you succeeded). 'manage' = 50 (past story: managed).

assessment.prompt: The interviewer says: 'Tell me about a time you worked under pressure.' Sari's answer includes this sentence: 'My job was to find a new supplier within two weeks, before our stock ran out.' Which STAR part is it? Write the letter (S, T, A or R).
acceptableAnswers: t
task
assessment.rubric: Correct: T (Task: what she had to do, her goal). 'task' written as a word = 100. 'S' = 30 (Situation is the background: where she worked, what was happening; this sentence is her goal). 'A' = 20 (she hasn't done anything yet). 'R' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Budi is telling the Action part of his STAR answer. Complete with the right form of 'contact': Last March, our app stopped working during a big sale, so I ___ the developer immediately.
acceptableAnswers: contacted
assessment.rubric: Correct: contacted (a finished past event in the story → past simple). 'have contacted' = 30 (the present perfect doesn't go with a finished time like last March). 'contact' = 20 (no tense marking: in English every event in a past story needs a past form). 'was contacting' = 40 (the past continuous is for the background, not the main action). 'called' or 'phoned' = 70 (good English, but the task asks for contact).

assessment.prompt: The interviewer asks: 'What would you say is your main strength?' Say it in English: Kekuatan utama saya adalah kerja sama tim.
acceptableAnswers: my main strength is teamwork
my main strength is team work
my biggest strength is teamwork
my greatest strength is teamwork
my key strength is teamwork
my main strength is working in a team
my main strength is working in teams
my main strength is my teamwork
my main strength is team working
my biggest strength is team work
my greatest strength is team work
assessment.rubric: Correct: My main strength is teamwork (biggest / greatest / key strength are also fine; working in a team is fine). 'My main strength is I'm good at teamwork' = 70 (understood, but needs 'that': My main strength is that I'm good at working in a team). 'My main strength is teamworks' = 70 (teamwork is uncountable). 'My main strengths is teamwork' = 60 (one strength → strength + is). 'I am teamwork' = 20.

assessment.prompt: At the end of your interview, the manager asks: 'Do you have any questions for us?' You want to know what you'll do every day in the job. Complete with one word: What does a typical ___ look like in this role?
acceptableAnswers: day
working day
workday
week
assessment.rubric: Correct: day (What does a typical day look like in this role?). 'working day', 'workday' and 'week' = 100. 'job' or 'work' = 40 (a typical job/work doesn't fit: you're asking about a normal day in this job). 'days' = 70 (a typical + singular: day).

assessment.prompt: The interviewer asks: 'Where do you see yourself in five years?' Say it in English, starting with 'In five years': Dalam lima tahun, saya ingin menjadi manajer proyek.
acceptableAnswers: in five years i'd like to be a project manager
in five years i would like to be a project manager
in five years i'd like to become a project manager
in five years i would like to become a project manager
in five years i'm hoping to be a project manager
in five years i am hoping to be a project manager
in five years i'm hoping to become a project manager
in five years i am hoping to become a project manager
in five years i hope to be a project manager
in five years i hope to become a project manager
in five years i want to be a project manager
in five years i want to become a project manager
in 5 years i'd like to be a project manager
in 5 years i would like to be a project manager
assessment.rubric: Correct: In five years, I'd like to be / become a project manager (I'm hoping to / I hope to are also good). 'I want to be' = 100 for meaning, but note that I'd like to sounds more polite in an interview. Missing 'a' (I'd like to be project manager) = 70 (a job needs a/an). 'I'd like to be a manager project' = 50 (word order: project manager, like manajer proyek reversed). 'I like to be a project manager' = 50 (I like = saya suka; I'd like = saya ingin).

blocks.text:
Almost every interview starts with ***Tell me about yourself*** or ***Can you tell me about your experience?*** Don't read your CV aloud. Use three parts:
- **Now:** ***I've been working as a sales executive at a bank in Surabaya for four years.*** (recap: **for** + a length of time, **since** + a starting point: *since 2021*)
- **Before:** ***Before that, I worked at an e-commerce company in Jakarta for two years.*** (finished → past simple)
- **Why this job:** ***Now I'm looking for a role with more responsibility.***

Then give **proof** (bukti). General words like *hard-working* or *I have a lot of experience* are easy to say and hard to believe. Concrete facts are better:
- ***I was responsible for*** + noun or -ing (bertanggung jawab atas): *I was responsible for the company's social media.*
- ***I managed to*** + verb (berhasil): *I managed to cut delivery costs by 15%.* Careful: ***manage*** + noun means memimpin / mengelola (*I managed a team of five*); ***managed to*** + verb means berhasil. Same word, two meanings.
- ***I led*** (memimpin; *lead – led – led*) ***a team of five.***
- **Numbers and results** with **by** + the amount (from the business vocabulary lesson): *increased sales **by** 20%*, *reduced complaints **by** half*, *trained 40 new staff*.

id.text:
Hampir setiap wawancara dimulai dengan ***Tell me about yourself*** (ceritakan tentang dirimu) atau ***Can you tell me about your experience?*** Jangan membacakan CV-mu. Pakai tiga bagian:
- **Sekarang:** ***I've been working as a sales executive at a bank in Surabaya for four years.*** (ulasan: **for** + lamanya waktu, **since** + titik mulai: *since 2021*)
- **Sebelumnya:** ***Before that, I worked at an e-commerce company in Jakarta for two years.*** (sudah selesai → past simple)
- **Kenapa pekerjaan ini:** ***Now I'm looking for a role with more responsibility.*** (sekarang saya mencari posisi dengan tanggung jawab yang lebih besar)

Lalu beri **bukti**. Kata-kata umum seperti *hard-working* (pekerja keras) atau *I have a lot of experience* mudah diucapkan tapi sulit dipercaya. Fakta yang konkret lebih baik:
- ***I was responsible for*** + kata benda atau -ing (bertanggung jawab atas): *I was responsible for the company's social media.*
- ***I managed to*** + kata kerja (berhasil): *I managed to cut delivery costs by 15%.* Hati-hati: ***manage*** + kata benda artinya memimpin / mengelola (*I managed a team of five*); ***managed to*** + kata kerja artinya berhasil. Kata yang sama, dua arti.
- ***I led*** (memimpin; *lead – led – led*) ***a team of five.***
- **Angka dan hasil** dengan **by** + jumlahnya (dari pelajaran kosakata bisnis): *increased sales **by** 20%* (menaikkan penjualan sebesar 20%), *reduced complaints **by** half* (mengurangi keluhan sampai separuhnya), *trained 40 new staff*.

blocks.text:
Four Indonesian traps:
- **`I have worked here since three years` ✗.** *sejak* isn't always *since*. *Three years* is a **length** of time → ***for three years***. *since* needs a **starting point**: *since 2022*, *since I graduated*.
- **`I succeeded to get 200 customers` ✗** (from *berhasil*). Say ***I managed to get …*** (*I succeeded in getting …* is also correct, but more formal).
- **`I was responsible to the project` ✗.** Say ***responsible for***.
- **`I have many experiences in marketing` ✗.** Work experience is uncountable: ***a lot of experience*** / ***five years of experience***. (*an experience* is one event: *Bali was a great experience.*)

Spelling: ***per cent*** (British) / ***percent*** (American). Both are fine; just be consistent.

id.text:
Empat jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia:
- **`I have worked here since three years` ✗.** *sejak* tidak selalu *since*. *Three years* adalah **lamanya** waktu → ***for three years***. *since* butuh **titik mulai**: *since 2022*, *since I graduated* (sejak saya lulus).
- **`I succeeded to get 200 customers` ✗** (dari *berhasil*). Katakan ***I managed to get …*** (*I succeeded in getting …* juga benar, tapi lebih formal).
- **`I was responsible to the project` ✗.** Katakan ***responsible for***.
- **`I have many experiences in marketing` ✗.** Pengalaman kerja tidak bisa dihitung: ***a lot of experience*** / ***five years of experience***. (*an experience* adalah satu kejadian: *Bali was a great experience.*)

Ejaan: ***per cent*** (British) / ***percent*** (Amerika). Dua-duanya boleh; yang penting konsisten.

blocks.prompt: The interviewer asks: 'Can you tell me about your experience in sales?' Which answer is the most convincing?
options: I have many experiences in sales, and I'm very hard-working.
I've been working in sales for four years, and last year I increased my team's sales by 20%.
Sales is very important for every company, so I like it.
blocks.explain: It says how long (*for four years*) and gives proof with a number (*increased … by 20%*). The first one has the *many experiences* mistake and no proof; the third one talks about sales in general, not about you.

id.prompt: Pewawancara bertanya: 'Can you tell me about your experience in sales?' Jawaban mana yang paling meyakinkan?
id.explain: Jawaban ini menyebut berapa lama (*for four years*) dan memberi bukti dengan angka (*increased … by 20%*). Jawaban pertama punya kesalahan *many experiences* dan tidak ada bukti; jawaban ketiga bicara soal penjualan secara umum, bukan tentang dirimu.

blocks.text:
A **behavioural question** (pertanyaan perilaku) asks what you **did** in a real situation, because past behaviour shows how you'll work in the future. You can recognise them by the start:
- ***Tell me about a time when you …*** (ceritakan saat kamu …)
- ***Give me an example of …***
- ***Describe a situation when you …***

Answer with **STAR**, four parts in order:
- **S = Situation** (situasinya): the background, short. When, where, what was your job? *Last year, I was working as …*
- **T = Task** (tugasnya): what you had to do or solve. *My manager asked me to … / I had to …*
- **A = Action** (tindakanmu): what **you** did, step by step. This is the **longest and most important** part. *First, I … Then I … I also …*
- **R = Result** (hasilnya): what happened in the end, with **numbers** if possible, and what you learnt. *As a result, … I learnt that …*

**Grammar:** it's a story, so use the **past simple** for the events (*I called, I moved, it fell*) and the **past continuous** for the background (*I was working as …*), as in the storytelling lesson. Spelling: *behavioural* (British) / *behavioral* (American); *learnt* (British) / *learned* (both).

id.text:
**Behavioural question** (pertanyaan perilaku) menanyakan apa yang **kamu lakukan** dalam situasi nyata, karena perilakumu di masa lalu menunjukkan bagaimana kamu akan bekerja nanti. Kamu bisa mengenalinya dari awal kalimatnya:
- ***Tell me about a time when you …*** (ceritakan saat kamu …)
- ***Give me an example of …*** (beri saya contoh …)
- ***Describe a situation when you …*** (gambarkan situasi saat kamu …)

Jawab dengan **STAR**, empat bagian secara berurutan:
- **S = Situation** (situasinya): latar belakangnya, singkat. Kapan, di mana, apa pekerjaanmu? *Last year, I was working as …*
- **T = Task** (tugasnya): apa yang harus kamu lakukan atau selesaikan. *My manager asked me to … / I had to …*
- **A = Action** (tindakanmu): apa yang **kamu** lakukan, langkah demi langkah. Ini bagian yang **paling panjang dan paling penting**. *First, I … Then I … I also …*
- **R = Result** (hasilnya): apa yang terjadi pada akhirnya, dengan **angka** kalau bisa, dan apa yang kamu pelajari. *As a result, … I learnt that …*

**Tata bahasa:** ini sebuah cerita, jadi pakai **past simple** untuk kejadiannya (*I called, I moved, it fell*) dan **past continuous** untuk latar belakangnya (*I was working as …*), seperti di pelajaran bercerita. Ejaan: *behavioural* (British) / *behavioral* (Amerika); *learnt* (British) / *learned* (keduanya).

rows.note: A = Action: what I did, step by step (the longest part)

id.note: A = Action: apa yang saya lakukan, langkah demi langkah (bagian terpanjang)

rows.en: As a result, the average waiting time fell from 70 to 25 minutes, and complaints dropped by half. I learnt that the data often shows the real problem.
rows.id: Hasilnya, rata-rata waktu tunggu turun dari 70 menjadi 25 menit, dan keluhan berkurang separuhnya. Saya belajar bahwa data sering menunjukkan masalah yang sebenarnya.
rows.note: R = Result: numbers, plus what I learnt

id.note: R = Result: angka, plus apa yang saya pelajari

blocks.text:
Three traps:
- **'Kami' everywhere.** Many of us say *we* or *our team* to be modest, and teamwork is a good thing. But the interviewer is hiring **you**, so in the Action part say what **you** did: ***Our team was very busy, so I personally called every customer.***
- **No past forms.** Indonesian verbs don't change, but an English story needs past forms: `Last year our app crash, so I call the developer` ✗ → ***Last year our app crashed, so I called the developer.***
- **A long Situation and no Result.** Keep S and T short (one or two sentences each), spend most of your time on A, and always finish with R. Aim for about one or two minutes in total.

id.text:
Tiga jebakan:
- **'Kami' di mana-mana.** Banyak dari kita bilang *we* atau *our team* supaya terdengar rendah hati, dan kerja sama tim itu bagus. Tapi pewawancara mau merekrut **kamu**, jadi di bagian Action katakan apa yang **kamu** lakukan: ***Our team was very busy, so I personally called every customer.*** (tim kami sangat sibuk, jadi saya sendiri yang menelepon setiap pelanggan)
- **Tanpa bentuk lampau.** Kata kerja bahasa Indonesia tidak berubah, tapi cerita dalam bahasa Inggris butuh bentuk lampau: `Last year our app crash, so I call the developer` ✗ → ***Last year our app crashed, so I called the developer.***
- **Situation panjang tanpa Result.** Buat S dan T singkat (masing-masing satu atau dua kalimat), habiskan sebagian besar waktumu di A, dan selalu akhiri dengan R. Targetkan sekitar satu atau dua menit secara keseluruhan.

blocks.prompt: Which STAR part is this sentence? 'So I made a checklist for the new staff and checked their work every afternoon for two weeks.'
blocks.explain: It says what the speaker **did**, step by step (*I made …, I checked …*): that's the **Action**. The Situation is the background, the Task is the goal, and the Result is what happened in the end.

id.prompt: Kalimat ini termasuk bagian STAR yang mana? 'So I made a checklist for the new staff and checked their work every afternoon for two weeks.'
id.explain: Kalimat ini menyebut apa yang **dilakukan** pembicara, langkah demi langkah (*I made …, I checked …*): itu **Action**. Situation adalah latar belakangnya, Task adalah tujuannya, dan Result adalah apa yang terjadi pada akhirnya.

material.title: Strengths and weaknesses: not too modest, not too proud

blocks.text:
**Strengths** (kekuatan, kelebihan): name **one** clear strength, then **prove it**.
- ***My main strength is*** + noun: *problem-solving, teamwork, attention to detail* (ketelitian).
- ***My main strength is that*** + sentence: *that I stay calm under pressure* (tetap tenang saat ditekan).
- ***I'm good at*** + noun or -ing: *I'm good at explaining technical things simply.*
- Then the proof: ***For example, …*** + a short true story with a number.

A long list (*I'm hard-working, smart, creative, friendly and honest*) proves nothing.

**Weaknesses** (kelemahan): the interviewer wants to see that you're honest and that you know yourself. Choose something **real** but not a disaster for this job, and say **what you're doing about it**:
- ***I sometimes find it hard to*** + verb: *say no to extra work / speak up in big meetings*.
- ***so I'm working on it by*** + -ing / ***so I've been taking an online course in …***

*I'm a perfectionist* is a cliché (sudah terlalu sering dipakai): interviewers hear it a lot. If it's true for you, add a real example.

id.text:
**Strengths** (kekuatan, kelebihan): sebutkan **satu** kekuatan yang jelas, lalu **buktikan**.
- ***My main strength is*** + kata benda: *problem-solving* (memecahkan masalah), *teamwork* (kerja sama tim), *attention to detail* (ketelitian).
- ***My main strength is that*** + kalimat: *that I stay calm under pressure* (tetap tenang saat ditekan).
- ***I'm good at*** + kata benda atau -ing: *I'm good at explaining technical things simply.*
- Lalu buktinya: ***For example, …*** + cerita singkat yang benar dengan angka.

Daftar panjang (*I'm hard-working, smart, creative, friendly and honest*) tidak membuktikan apa pun.

**Weaknesses** (kelemahan): pewawancara ingin melihat bahwa kamu jujur dan mengenal dirimu sendiri. Pilih sesuatu yang **nyata** tapi tidak fatal untuk pekerjaan ini, dan katakan **apa yang sedang kamu lakukan untuk memperbaikinya**:
- ***I sometimes find it hard to*** + kata kerja (kadang saya sulit …): *say no to extra work / speak up in big meetings*.
- ***so I'm working on it by*** + -ing / ***so I've been taking an online course in …***

*I'm a perfectionist* itu klise (sudah terlalu sering dipakai): pewawancara sering mendengarnya. Kalau itu memang benar untukmu, tambahkan contoh nyata.

rows.en: My main strength is that I stay calm under pressure. For example, when our system went down during Ramadan sales, I handled 80 customer chats in one evening.
rows.id: Kekuatan utama saya adalah saya tetap tenang saat ditekan. Contohnya, waktu sistem kami mati saat promo Ramadan, saya menangani 80 chat pelanggan dalam satu malam.

rows.en: I'm good at explaining technical things simply. Last year, I trained 40 new staff on our new system.
rows.id: Saya pandai menjelaskan hal teknis dengan sederhana. Tahun lalu, saya melatih 40 staf baru untuk sistem baru kami.

rows.en: I sometimes find it hard to say no to extra work, so I'm learning to agree on priorities with my manager.
rows.id: Kadang saya sulit menolak pekerjaan tambahan, jadi saya sedang belajar menyepakati prioritas dengan manajer saya.

rows.en: My writing in English isn't perfect yet, so I've been taking an online business writing course.
rows.id: Tulisan bahasa Inggris saya belum sempurna, jadi saya sedang ikut kursus online menulis untuk bisnis.
rows.note: honest + what you're doing about it

id.note: jujur + apa yang sedang kamu lakukan untuk memperbaikinya

blocks.text:
Two habits to watch, in both directions:
- **Too modest (the 'saya masih belajar' style).** In Indonesian culture, being humble (rendah hati) is polite: *Maaf, bahasa Inggris saya kurang bagus, saya masih belajar, saya cuma staf biasa.* In an English interview this can sound like you don't have the skills or don't believe in yourself. *I'm still learning about data analysis* is fine **if you then say what you can already do**: *…, but I've already built our monthly sales dashboard.*
- **Too proud (overclaiming).** *I'm the best salesperson in Indonesia. I can do everything. I'm expert in all software.* This is hard to believe and can sound arrogant.

The middle way: **facts and numbers**. Let them speak for you.

id.text:
Dua kebiasaan yang perlu diperhatikan, ke dua arah:
- **Terlalu merendah (gaya 'saya masih belajar').** Dalam budaya Indonesia, rendah hati itu sopan: *Maaf, bahasa Inggris saya kurang bagus, saya masih belajar, saya cuma staf biasa.* Di wawancara berbahasa Inggris, ini bisa terdengar seperti kamu tidak punya kemampuannya atau tidak percaya pada dirimu sendiri. *I'm still learning about data analysis* boleh saja **asal kamu lalu menyebut apa yang sudah bisa kamu lakukan**: *…, but I've already built our monthly sales dashboard.*
- **Terlalu membanggakan diri (overclaiming).** *I'm the best salesperson in Indonesia. I can do everything. I'm expert in all software.* Ini sulit dipercaya dan bisa terdengar sombong.

Jalan tengahnya: **fakta dan angka**. Biarkan itu yang berbicara untukmu.

blocks.prompt: Your English is good, but not perfect. The interviewer asks: 'How is your English?' Which answer is best?
options: Sorry, my English is very bad. I'm still learning.
My English is perfect, like a native speaker.
I use English every day with our clients in Singapore, and I'm taking an online course to improve my writing.
blocks.explain: It's honest and confident: facts (*every day with our clients*) plus what you're doing to improve. The first answer is too modest and makes the interviewer doubt you; the second is overclaiming and easy to test.

id.prompt: Bahasa Inggrismu bagus, tapi tidak sempurna. Pewawancara bertanya: 'How is your English?' Jawaban mana yang paling baik?
id.explain: Jawaban ini jujur dan percaya diri: ada fakta (*every day with our clients*) plus apa yang sedang kamu lakukan untuk memperbaikinya. Jawaban pertama terlalu merendah dan membuat pewawancara ragu padamu; jawaban kedua berlebihan dan mudah diuji.

id.title: Kekuatan dan kelemahan: jangan terlalu merendah, jangan terlalu membanggakan diri

material.title: Career goals, your questions, and what to leave out

blocks.text:
**Career goals.** *Where do you see yourself in five years?* The interviewer wants to know if you have a plan and if it fits the company.
- ***In five years, I'd like to*** + verb: *lead a small team / become a project manager*.
- ***I'm hoping to*** + verb: *get a certificate in cloud computing*.
- ***My long-term goal is to*** + verb (tujuan jangka panjang).

*I'd like to* sounds more polite than *I want to*. Saying *I don't know* sounds like you have no plan.

**Your questions.** At the end you'll hear ***Do you have any questions for us?*** Always ask one or two. *No, I don't have any questions* can sound like you're not really interested.
- ***What does a typical day look like in this role?***
- ***What are the biggest challenges for the team right now?***
- ***What training do new staff get?***
- ***What are the next steps in the process?***

Salary and leave (gaji dan cuti) usually come later in the process, or when the interviewer brings them up. That's a tendency: it depends on the company and the country.

id.text:
**Tujuan karier.** *Where do you see yourself in five years?* (di mana kamu melihat dirimu lima tahun lagi?) Pewawancara ingin tahu apakah kamu punya rencana dan apakah rencana itu cocok dengan perusahaannya.
- ***In five years, I'd like to*** + kata kerja: *lead a small team / become a project manager*.
- ***I'm hoping to*** + kata kerja (saya berharap bisa): *get a certificate in cloud computing*.
- ***My long-term goal is to*** + kata kerja (tujuan jangka panjang).

*I'd like to* terdengar lebih sopan daripada *I want to*. Menjawab *I don't know* terdengar seperti kamu tidak punya rencana.

**Pertanyaanmu.** Di akhir kamu akan mendengar ***Do you have any questions for us?*** Selalu ajukan satu atau dua pertanyaan. *No, I don't have any questions* bisa terdengar seperti kamu tidak terlalu tertarik.
- ***What does a typical day look like in this role?*** (seperti apa hari kerja biasa di posisi ini?)
- ***What are the biggest challenges for the team right now?*** (apa tantangan terbesar tim saat ini?)
- ***What training do new staff get?*** (pelatihan apa yang didapat staf baru?)
- ***What are the next steps in the process?*** (apa tahap berikutnya dalam proses ini?)

Gaji dan cuti biasanya dibahas di tahap berikutnya, atau saat pewawancara yang mengangkatnya. Itu kecenderungan: tergantung perusahaan dan negaranya.

rows.en: In five years, I'd like to lead a small marketing team here.
rows.id: Dalam lima tahun, saya ingin memimpin tim pemasaran kecil di sini.

rows.en: I'm hoping to get a certificate in cloud computing next year.
rows.id: Saya berharap bisa mendapat sertifikat cloud computing tahun depan.

rows.en: My long-term goal is to become a product manager.
rows.id: Tujuan jangka panjang saya adalah menjadi product manager.

rows.en: What training do new staff get in the first month?
rows.id: Pelatihan apa yang didapat staf baru di bulan pertama?

rows.en: What are the next steps in the process?
rows.id: Apa tahap berikutnya dalam proses ini?

blocks.text: **Personal information.** Many Indonesian CVs include religion, marital status, age and a photo, and some interviewers in Indonesia ask about them: that's normal here. In many other countries (the UK, the US, Australia), interviewers usually avoid these topics, because the hiring decision shouldn't depend on them. So in an English interview, especially with a company abroad, you don't need to mention them unprompted. Talk about your skills and experience instead. If an interviewer does ask, a short, polite answer is fine.

id.text: **Informasi pribadi.** Banyak CV di Indonesia mencantumkan agama, status pernikahan, usia dan foto, dan sebagian pewawancara di Indonesia menanyakannya: itu hal yang biasa di sini. Di banyak negara lain (Inggris, Amerika, Australia), pewawancara biasanya menghindari topik-topik ini, karena keputusan merekrut tidak boleh bergantung pada hal itu. Jadi di wawancara berbahasa Inggris, terutama dengan perusahaan di luar negeri, kamu tidak perlu menyebutnya kalau tidak ditanya. Bicarakan kemampuan dan pengalamanmu saja. Kalau pewawancara memang bertanya, jawaban singkat yang sopan sudah cukup.

blocks.prompt: You're in an online interview with a company in Sydney. The interviewer says: 'So, tell me about yourself.' Which start is best?
options: I'm 28 years old, I'm Muslim, and I'm not married yet.
I'm a data analyst with three years of experience in e-commerce.
I'm nobody special, just a normal staff.
blocks.explain: Start with your job and your experience: that's what the interviewer needs. Age, religion and marital status usually aren't part of an interview in Australia, so you don't need to mention them. The third one is far too modest (and *a staff* isn't natural English: say *a member of staff* or *an employee*).

id.prompt: Kamu sedang wawancara online dengan sebuah perusahaan di Sydney. Pewawancara berkata: 'So, tell me about yourself.' Pembuka mana yang paling baik?
id.explain: Mulailah dengan pekerjaan dan pengalamanmu: itu yang dibutuhkan pewawancara. Usia, agama dan status pernikahan biasanya bukan bagian dari wawancara di Australia, jadi kamu tidak perlu menyebutnya. Pilihan ketiga jauh terlalu merendah (dan *a staff* tidak wajar dalam bahasa Inggris: katakan *a member of staff* atau *an employee*).

resources.note: Practical advice: study the job description, prepare examples for common questions (strengths and weaknesses), research the company, and prepare your own questions. It also covers what to bring and online interviews.

id.note: Saran praktis: pelajari deskripsi pekerjaannya, siapkan contoh untuk pertanyaan umum (kekuatan dan kelemahan), cari tahu tentang perusahaannya, dan siapkan pertanyaanmu sendiri. Artikel ini juga membahas apa yang perlu dibawa dan wawancara online.

id.intro: Kamu sudah bisa presentasi, ikut rapat dan menyebut sudah berapa lama kamu melakukan sesuatu. Sekarang kamu akan memakai semua itu dalam **wawancara kerja**: menjelaskan pengalamanmu dengan contoh konkret dan angka, menjawab pertanyaan 'Tell me about a time …' dengan **metode STAR**, dan membicarakan kekuatanmu, satu kelemahan dan tujuan kariermu. Pemanasan: apa satu hal di tempat kerja atau di kampus yang kamu banggakan?
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana cara membicarakan kelemahan tanpa terdengar buruk?
Bisa bantu aku menyusun jawaban STAR tentang pekerjaanku sebelumnya?
Apakah tidak sopan menanyakan gaji di wawancara pertama?
Kapan aku pakai 'for' dan kapan 'since' untuk pengalamanku?

assessment.ji-1: Dalam wawancara di sebuah bank di Surabaya, Dimas mengucapkan kalimat ini, tapi ada kesalahannya. Tulis kalimat yang benar: I've been working here since six years.
assessment.ji-2: Di pekerjaanmu sebelumnya, mendapat 200 pelanggan baru dalam tiga bulan itu sulit, tapi kamu berhasil. Lengkapi dengan satu kata yang berarti 'berhasil': After a lot of hard work, I ___ to get 200 new customers in three months.
assessment.ji-3: Pewawancara berkata: 'Tell me about a time you worked under pressure.' Jawaban Sari memuat kalimat ini: 'My job was to find a new supplier within two weeks, before our stock ran out.' Kalimat itu bagian STAR yang mana? Tulis hurufnya (S, T, A atau R).
assessment.ji-4: Budi sedang menceritakan bagian Action dari jawaban STAR-nya. Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'contact': Last March, our app stopped working during a big sale, so I ___ the developer immediately.
assessment.ji-5: Pewawancara bertanya: 'What would you say is your main strength?' Katakan dalam bahasa Inggris: Kekuatan utama saya adalah kerja sama tim.
assessment.ji-6: Di akhir wawancara, manajernya bertanya: 'Do you have any questions for us?' Kamu ingin tahu apa yang akan kamu kerjakan setiap hari di pekerjaan itu. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: What does a typical ___ look like in this role?
assessment.ji-7: Pewawancara bertanya: 'Where do you see yourself in five years?' Katakan dalam bahasa Inggris, mulai dengan 'In five years': Dalam lima tahun, saya ingin menjadi manajer proyek.
